notes: Copilot runs foreground subagents IN-PROCESS: subagent.started/subagent.completed pair on toolCallId inside the parent's events.jsonl and no session-state/<child>/ directory is ever created. So the claudecode/opencode phase shape (child_session_birth as transcript_new + parent_linked) is not merely absent here, it is unreachable — there is no child SessionState to link. What this spec CAN assert is the arc the scenario's process section actually turns on: the parent goes ready→working at spawn, is HELD working across the child's lifetime (both subagent events are Skip=true in parser.go:390, and Copilot's only turn boundary is the explicit assistant.turn_end), and returns working→ready only after the subagent has completed. KNOWN FAILING, and NOT expressible as a phase: SubagentCount(parent) must read 1 between the two subagent events, but agents.SubagentCounters (maps.go:137-153) closes over a parser instance created at wiring time while the metrics adapter tails with a different per-transcript instance (adapter.go:78-86, :123), so session.SessionMetrics.OpenSubagents is always 0 — probe through the real collector seen red at 'domain OpenSubagents = 0, want 1'. expected.jsonl's DSL matches only state_transition states and lifecycle kinds and ObservationSpec covers model/cost/tokens, so there is no predicate for a subagent count; the flag plus the assessment body are the record of the broken half, and the phases below deliberately assert the CORRECT behaviour of the half that works. Single-birth adapter (agent.FilesUnderRoot + sessionIDFromPath keys the session to its session-state/<id>/ dir), so the birth is one phase anchored to start UNPINNED. duration_at_least_ms on the working phase is what bounds the held-working invariant window — 5000ms is a floor chosen well under a realistic gpt-5-mini subagent span, not the span itself. model is left unpinned (--model accepts only "auto"; the effective model is resolved at runtime via session.auto_mode_resolved) and cost is unasserted (gpt-5-mini has no core/pkg/capacity/aliases.go entry) — record fills both from the recording.

text: The copilot session appears in ready once session-state/<id>/events.jsonl is written

The delegation prompt drives the session ready → working (spec bullet 1), and it STAYS working across the subagent's lifetime — it neither settles to ready nor drops into waiting while the child runs (spec bullet 4). subagent.started/subagent.completed are Skip=true and are not themselves state changes.
After the subagent reports back and the parent replies 'done', the explicit assistant.turn_end fires: working → ready (spec bullet 5 — only after the last child ends)
